I am 52. I left school after junior high and started farming full-time at 17. My father taught me the basics, and the rest I learned by doing and watching the neighbors. My farm is 7.5 mu — not tiny, but not big either. Three people at home, so every yuan matters.

This year I will do mostly what I did last year because last year was okay. I don't change things that work. Fertilizer prices are high again, but I would rather put a little too much than lose yield. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost you absorb.

On my 3 mu of cabbage-chili land: I plant spring cabbage first. I buy hybrid cabbage seeds from the dealer — the same kind Old Wang used last year, his cabbages looked good. For each mu, I spread two cartloads of manure and one 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer as base. Then I top-dress twice with urea, about 15 kg each time. That is about 25 kg of nitrogen per mu total. I irrigate six times — planting water, then every couple of weeks if it doesn't rain. I spray pesticide four times, mainly for caterpillars and aphids. I hire the rotary tiller to work the soil. I expect about 4,500 kg per mu, same as last year.

After I harvest the cabbage in June, I plant chili on that same 3 mu. I buy hybrid chili seedlings from the market — raising them myself is too much trouble. Quick rotary till, then base fertilizer: manure plus one bag of compound per mu. Chili needs more potassium, so I add extra potash. Top-dress three times. Total nitrogen about 20 kg per mu, potassium about 15 kg. Chili needs water, so I irrigate eight times. Spray six times because chili gets aphids and virus easy. Expect 2,500 kg per mu of fresh chili.

My 2 mu of eggplant: hybrid seedlings, same base fertilizer as cabbage — one bag compound plus manure per mu. Top-dress twice. Nitrogen about 18 kg, phosphorus 8 kg, potassium 12 kg per mu. Seven irrigations. Five pesticide sprays. Should get 3,500 kg per mu.

My 1.5 mu of kidney bean: I use improved seeds I saved from last year. Less fertilizer — half a bag of compound per mu, top-dress once. Nitrogen 10 kg, phosphorus 5 kg, potassium 8 kg per mu. Five irrigations. Three sprays. Yield about 1,800 kg per mu.

My 1 mu of maize: hybrid seeds, bought new. Mainly for household feed. One bag compound as base, one top-dress of urea. Nitrogen 18 kg, phosphorus 6 kg, potassium 5 kg per mu. Three irrigations. Two sprays for armyworm. Expect 600 kg per mu.

I use the rotary tiller for everything. Plowing costs too much and takes too long. My well can handle 7.5 mu if I schedule watering carefully.

I watch my neighbors. If Old Wang adds more fertilizer, I think about adding more. If everyone is spraying for disease, I spray too. Better safe than sorry.
